result:
## 1. The seal argument

- **Verdict.** I found no counterexample inside H1 + H2 with a globally sealed roster. Argument 1 is true but not a proof as written; argument 2 holds; the real hole is HOLD.
- **Argument 1, repairs needed.**
  - It is circular as worded: "every birth's parents lie among the descendants of one part" is the conclusion. Make it one induction on rounds with a joint invariant: every knot made after s descends from exactly one part, and holds only Δ of that part plus that part's fresh distinctions.
  - State two lemmas it uses silently: holders never decrease and a barred distinction is never unbarred, so a non-member never becomes a member. Run B(ii) violates the first.
  - Say "descendants of members" in the conclusion, not "members".
- **The hypothesis can be weakened, which removes the drafter's worry.** Link two members when they hold a common distinction or some knot meets both. The components (unions of parts) play the role of "sealed roster".
  - The same proof shows two such classes never share a distinction, never become joinable and never have a joint birth, under H1 + H2 with any release rule.
  - Pairwise "sealed apart" is not enough: X and Y can each share with a third part Z.
- **Argument 2 (hand-checked).**
  - Three or more holders: any third holder meets both, so they are one part.
  - Exactly two holders: under H1 they are parent and child, or two start knots.
  - Under RELEASE every acting member spends everything, including under CANCEL-OFFSHOOT and TAKE-SHARED (a short member owes more than h, so all h go).
  - A waiting member has no children yet, so its shared distinctions gain holders only through its own later births.
  - The exception does not occur on the registered starts after round 0: Ring(5, 3) members owe 2 and hold 3.
- **H1 and H2 for Q, TAKE-SHARED, INHERIT.** Satisfied under every index, because the index only chooses among a parent's own places.
- **Argument 3 overreaches.** "Any release rule" is unproved under HOLD with pairwise sealing; I expect a meeting through a third part to be possible under Q + HOLD (not constructed). Reword to classes, or restrict to RELEASE.
- **Argument 4, omissions.**
  - The 5,000-knot stop and any engine guard fire at different rounds in runs A and B.
  - LITERAL is switched off everywhere by any barred distinction (shared definitions lines 73–74), and B(i) always bars. A paired LITERAL test compares closing-on with closing-off.
  - The names claim needs "sorted" to mean lexicographic on knot names; then the renaming between runs preserves order.
- **Argument 5.** Sound. Add that structural joinability is handled by argument 1 run in the same induction.

## 2. The definitions

- **Order of births.** "Sorted" by what? Say lexicographic on sorted member names. Also say which loose distinction goes to which birth, and when knot and fresh names are assigned (fresh counts are known only after demand).
- **"At the start of the round".** It fixes eligibility. Say that several births may take the same distinction in one round, and that a distinction loose at the start is never eligible.
- **TAKE-SHARED.** Mostly implementable (hand-checked on the three-knot start; it gives h2). Missing: that the short member makes no offshoots, and that a residual stall repeats for ever.
- **AT(k).**
  - No ancestor k steps up: undefined. The smallest case needs "no take".
  - No eligible distinction: say "no take".
  - Several ancestors k steps up: undefined, and it decides a headline. Hand work on the CANCEL-WAIT case: offshoots 18 and 19 of knot 16 (child of join 3) have knots 1 and 2 both two steps up. Union + oldest gives distinction 0 and the meeting "through knot 1"; preferring knot 2 gives distinction 2 and it meets the other copy instead. With 0 it also goes through start knot 0.
  - Say why joins do not take, and whether a short member's offshoots do.
- **NEAR.** Ties among equally near ancestors; "children" read from the record; LINES after lines have joined; LONE before or after cancellation. Also LINES counts *member* descendants, so barring Y changes the trigger: it reads Y directly, like PARTS.
- **INHERIT.** A join takes one per parent, which contradicts "every rung takes at most one extra per birth".
- **Section 3.3 table.** Q is marked "ancestor-taking: yes", but the definition says "an ancestor of one of its parents". Q and INHERIT are parent-taking.
- **SIB.** Undefined for joins and for TAKE-SHARED (the allowed set differs per birth). With one offshoot per parent it equals O, as in the smallest case.
- **FRESH.**
  - Zero- or one-based counting is unstated.
  - "Places less parents" is not "what it received" once a knot has taken extras.
  - It reads the number of parents, which is the record, not the structure.
  - Hand work, smallest case: parent 6 gives 3 − 1 = 2; allowed are 0, 1, 4, 5; zero-based picks 4, held by knots 1 and 3. Knot 3 is not an ancestor, so "held only by its own ancestors" is wrong under that reading.
  - If both copies use FRESH, 12 and 13 take 4 and 14 and 15 take 6, and they are one part again through the retired join 3, a knot the growth made. Register it.
- **Fresh by inputs.** Say that inputs are counted as distinct distinctions.
- **ELIMINATION.** Is each birth tested against the structure before the round, or are the round's births tested in sequence? The order matters. Also drop "only birth, nothing barred" explicitly.
- **Sealed apart.** The first clause is empty: a knot meeting a member of each makes them joinable. It reduces to "no member of X holds a distinction a member of Y holds".
- **Met set.** State that a knot is not in its own met set; the two-knot start depends on it.
- **Meets again.** In the smallest case knots 12 and 14 never meet (hand-checked); they are joinable through knot 0. The word uses "meet" in a second sense (see 8).
- **Returns.** Line 85 requires "past its start". Under Q-O the members meet, so "never returns" may hold by definition. P3 should keep its own sameness test and say so.
- **Run B(ii).** Not well formed in general.
  - Under AT(k), other knots may hold distinctions first held by Y's members.
  - Under HOLD, Y's members have children.
  - Un-sharing changes the allowed count. Hand work: removing waiting knot 3 makes distinction 4 loose, so FRESH counts modulo 3 instead of 4 and X's take changes, a spurious grade 2.
  - Define it only when no other knot holds a distinction Y first held or took; otherwise report "not defined".
- **Course.**
  - A joint birth is excluded but its children are included; say so.
  - "Met sets among them" means intersected with X's descendants.
  - Per-round multisets can miss differences; also register exact equality of X's trace under the order-preserving renaming.
- **Channels.** See 3.
- **"First eight parts".** The order is unstated.
- **"Founder" and "copy".** Used but not defined.

## 3. The paired test and the grades

- **Soundness.** B(i) tests "Y stops growing"; the owner said "without it". Barred Y is invisible to X's groups, so B(i) is the cleaner primary. Tell him B(ii) is only partly definable.
- **Spurious grade 2.**
  - The bounds and guard: compare only to the last round both runs reached.
  - LITERAL: do not pair under it.
  - B(ii) un-sharing.
  - The NEAR triggers.
  - A third part Z changed by Y and later reaching X: real but indirect; label it.
  - Names, order of births and demand are clean, given the fixes in 2.
- **Demand.** Keep it out of the course, since the owner said "builds". Report the first round at which X's demand differs as its own line. Hand work: in the smallest case that is round 3 (knot 12 has demand 3 against 1), one round before grade 2.
- **Channel classification.** Not sound as drafted. Being in one part at round t − 1 or t is co-occurrence, and it misses meetings earlier than t − 1. Make it causal:
  - Compare X's full trace step by step and classify by the first differing step: a round-wide trigger, a take, or a group or owing.
  - Confirm "meeting" with a third run that ignores groups containing descendants of both; the difference must vanish.
- **Supplied or made.**
  - Item 3's second disjunct is satisfied by every take, so it cannot fail.
  - Item 2 passes the smallest case although the meeting goes through the start's own common knot of the founders.
  - Use three verdicts: through a knot the growth made; through a start knot (the start's meeting reopened); supplied (global, rule, record-only).
  - O is a bias toward the start: "oldest name" reaches the start's distinctions as the start happens to be numbered. Register a start-renaming swap. Hand prediction: with names reversed, O behaves as N and the smallest case vanishes.
- **Grade 3 by the index.** Y does not differ, so it is not grade 3 by the draft's own definition. It is close to a tautology (the take is the only link), but it is a useful control. Report it as "the choice is necessary".
- **The grades are not a scale.** The smallest case has 2 without 1; grades 0 and 1 are facts about run A, 2 and 3 are comparisons.

## 4. The ladder

- **AT(k).** "Exactly k" is contrived, and nothing motivates k = 2 over "at most k".
- **The ordering.** It is not an order: RECORD-k reads k record steps and sits lowest, INHERIT reads one and sits above Q. "Least rung" has meaning only on the chain Q, AT(1), AT(2).
  - Use a cost vector (holder steps, record steps, roster-wide readings, source of the choice) and report every minimal law.
  - Cut NEAR to one control; three variants are forking paths.
- **A cheaper record-free law exists.** Register it as rung 1½, between Q and AT(1); under a holder-step order it comes first outside H1. Proposed name MET.
  - Offshoot clause: an offshoot also takes one distinction, chosen by the choice rule, that is shared at the start of the round, is held by a knot its parent meets, and is not held by the parent.
  - Join clause: a join also takes one shared distinction of a common knot of its parents that no parent holds.
  - "That is not its parent" would need the record; drop it.
  - After the start, while members meet only their parents, the offshoot clause is AT(1). So AT(1)'s cost of "k + 1 record steps" is overstated.
- **Hand prediction: three-knot start, (FLOOR1, CANCEL-RETIRE, RELEASE), by inputs, oldest.**
  - Round 1: join 3 takes nothing extra (every distinction of knot 0 is held by a parent). Offshoot 4 takes 5 and 2; offshoot 5 takes 7 and 0; each gets one fresh.
  - Knots 1 and 2 each meet 3, 4 and 5, so there are three pairs and no group of three.
  - Round 2: each owes 2 and holds 1; all retire. Stopped at 6 knots, nothing comes apart, no pair to test. Newest gives the same.
  - Under CANCEL-WAIT it jams at round 2.
  - It links the two sides too early to ask the question on this start. Register it on the other starts with no prediction.
- **Demand-reading ration.** Yes: register CAP-3 with the B-COPY treatments in the ladder runs as a swap, with open predictions. Not ORD, which is unbounded with many holders. It is the only registered place a meeting could feed a joint birth.

## 5. The predictions

- **True by construction** (code checks): P0; P1 and P2 under RELEASE; P6.
  - P0 should say "connected" for the agreement of the closings.
- **Replication of the prototype only:** P3, P4, P7, P8, P9, P11.
  - Hand-confirmed: P4, and P7 rounds 1 to 4 (not the knot tests).
  - P9 depends on the FRESH counting; P8 depends on the channel rule and the tie rule.
- **Not decidable as registered.**
  - P5: run 2 has no paired test, and the paired test is defined only for sealed-apart pairs.
  - P3 where Q-O exceeds the bounds (the prototype stopped 33 runs): say "through the last round read".
  - P8's "NEAR adds no cheaper case" has no meaning.
- **Expected to fail.**
  - P11 under parity at 10 rounds and 5,000 knots: the three-parent-join failure is not specific to NEAR.
  - P5 if it is made decidable: a joint birth removes a birth from X's course.
  - P1 under HOLD (see 1).
- **What the owner asked for.**
  - (a) Partly. The A225 move gets only a conditional verdict and no run; register one hand-placed A225 birth on both objects as a supplied control. Under Q and TAKE-SHARED the objects are destroyed (no return, no two-knot part), and Q-O, Q-SIB and TAKE-SHARED had no pair to test, so arm A's evidence is nearly empty and rests on the argument. Say so, and register taking that begins after the copies exist.
  - (b) Partly. The two-knot start's own two parts are unsealed at round 0, so the paired test excludes his most literal case. Allow labelled unsealed pairs.
  - (c) Not met: not-all-equal to 400 knots, parity to 3,000, runs to 5,000; runs 2 and 4 list no knot test. Lower the bounds or state the shortfall.
  - (d) Named, but not swapped in the ladder: order of births, the demand reading after takes, fresh by parents, HOLD, the rations.
  - (e) Present but cannot fail (see 3).
  - (f) Present but "least" is undefined, and the record-free law is missing.
  - (g) Met, except "the knot of the owner's picture" in the scope section, when the smallest case has none.
  - (h) Met, with two errors: FRESH reads the record, and O and N read how the start is numbered.

## 6. The eight open questions

1. Right in substance. "Sealed" is stronger than needed and awkward under HOLD; use the classes of "shares a distinction or is joinable", and count the prototype's HOLD meetings against those.
2. Keep the question on parts that share nothing. Register HOLD as a separate arm with a paired test on unsealed pairs. Tell the owner his premise holds under RELEASE only.
3. Yes, without demand. Report the first differing demand beside it.
4. No. Classify by the first differing step of the trace and confirm with the cross-group-masked run.
5. AT(1) is essentially that law after the start. Register the record-free form as its own rung, and order by a cost vector.
6. No. The approved definition says ancestor. Report "start common knot of the founders" as its own class and ask the owner.
7. Yes: CAP-3 as a registered swap.
8. Yes, and not-all-equal stays primary overall. Fix the within-round order of ELIMINATION, count implied births that fail as failures, and keep LITERAL out of paired tests.

## 7. Scope and honesty

- **A positive would show** that a supplied rule reaching back along descent can put two separated copies in one part, and that the first then builds differently. In the smallest case, with Y barred the first copy makes a three-parent join; with Y present two of its members retire and it makes one offshoot.
- **It would not show** a reference. One bit crosses (present or not), by crowding. Nothing is built jointly, the meeting is through the start's dead knot and not an ancestor, and it disappears under "newest" or a renumbered start.
- **Is the phrase honest?** "A part whose course depends on another" is literally true. "Reads" and "made by the growth" are not earned.
- **Plain sentence for the owner.** "Under the three recorded laws, no, and we can say why: a birth that takes only what its own parents hold can never reach a part that shares nothing with it. If a birth may also take a distinction from a knot two steps back in its own descent, two separated copies do become one part again and the first then builds differently. But in the smallest case they come back through the start's dead knot, the second copy only stops two of the first copy's members, and we supplied the rule, the choice of distinction and the record of descent. No part has yet built anything from another."
- **Literature (from memory, unchecked).**
  - A reference "k binders up" is a de Bruijn index (de Bruijn 1972); in compilers, the static link followed k times.
  - "Take from a knot the parent meets" is the embedding step of node-replacement graph grammars (NLC, Janssens and Rozenberg, about 1980).
  - Sharing in term-graph rewriting: Barendregt and others, 1987.
  - Lindenmayer's 1968 papers already included interaction; the names 0L and IL are later.

## 8. Words

| Word | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| ancestral common knot | Keep. |
| root | No. The birth record is not a tree (a join has two parents), and "root of an equation" is in use. For descent alone: "common ancestor". |
| ancestor-taking | Keep, for AT upward only; Q and INHERIT are "parent-taking". |
| take | Keep. |
| sealed apart; sealed | "Share nothing". "Disjoint" is wrong (parts are always disjoint as sets); "clean apart" is vague. |
| meets again | "One part again" and "one part for the first time". "Meet" is already what two knots do, and these members do not meet. Quote the owner's phrase in the question only. |
| the index | "The choice". The owner's index says which part of another pattern is looked at; this is a tie-break among one knot's places. Keep his word for his sense. |
| course | Keep. |
| grade | Not a scale. "Mark", or name the four. |
| channel | "Way"; the study speaks of one bit crossing, so the information-theory sense is too close. |
| parent step | Keep. |
| the descendants of g | Keep; write "X and its descendants" where the members are included. |
| reads | Reserved for the owner's sense, yet the draft uses it for rules, rungs and the engine. Use "uses" or "looks at". |
| B-RING, B-COPY | RING-LAW, COPY-LAW ("B" is also run B and arm B). |
| TAKE-SHARED | SHORT-TAKES (every law here takes shared). |
| INHERIT | CARRY (heredity and a settled programming sense). |
| AT(k) | STEPS-k. |
| NEAR | A space word; FIRST(trigger). |
| RECORD-k | Keep. |
| ANY | ALL-JOINABLE (ANY is taken, shared definitions line 110). |
| O, N | OLDEST, NEWEST (N(t) is the count of two-knot parts). |
| SIB | IN-TURN. |
| FRESH | BY-COUNT. |
| EVERY | ALL-CHOICES. |
| LINES | TWO-CHILDREN ("line" is a space word and was avoided). |
| ELIMINATION | IMPLIED. |
| h1, h2, h3 | Rename; they differ from H1, H2 only by case. |
